title: Fantasy football Week 5 risers and fallers: Jared Goff rises to QB1 - CBS Sports
description: Heath Cummings breaks down the biggest risers and fallers in his rankings after running through his Week 5 projec
body:
Heath Cummings breaks down the biggest risers and fallers in his rankings after running through his Week 5 projections
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:49 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We've got four weeks of football under our belts, which should mean we are starting to feel more certain about player roles and performance. That would probably be more true if we didn't lose a handful of stars to injury seemingly every week. Still, I feel confident saying we know a lot more now than we did a month ago. This newfound knowledge comes just in time for the first byes of the season. Normally, a two-team bye week is worthy of a yawn, but in Week 5, we'll be missing two top 12 quarterbacks, two top 12 running backs, a top 12 receiver, and a top 12 tight end. In other words, we've got work to do.One thing I hope to avoid as I do this weekly is calling a guy a faller one week and a riser the next week. But we had a lot of guys that we all but gave up on after three bad weeks who finally popped. At the very least, we have to address some of those, starting with Malik Nabers. We also have some big matchup shifts, which always impact the weekly projections.Prominent players, we had projected last week that we are not projecting to play in Week 5 as of Monday evening: Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley, Ladd McConkey, DJ, Moore, Kyle Monangai, Mack Hollins, Marcus Mariota
At the bottom of this article are my Week 5 projections for quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and tight end. They will be updated throughout the week as we get more information. Risers Jared Goff, QB, LionsThe first thing that is going to stand out to you is that Jared Goff is QB1 for Week 5. I'm not sure it should be that big of a surprise. He is QB5 on a per-game basis for the season, and he's facing a Cardinals defense that has given up the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing defenses. I could make the argument that they have been the worst pass defense in the league, but if they haven't, it may be Goff's Lions. Goff's Lions have an implied total of 29, which is both the biggest number on the weekend and slightly below their season average. It also helps Goff's case that Josh Allen is on the road against the Rams without DJ Moore.Drake Maye, QB, PatriotsMaye is the first of the Week 4 rebounds who also rebound in my projections. His Patriots are 3.5-point favorites at home against the Raiders, and I mostly buy that Maye and the Patriots' pass game found something last week. He's not in the QB1 discussion like we thought he might be this system, but he does project as a QB1, and I would start him over most, if not all, of the streaming options. Maye ranks second behind only Lamar Jackson in quarterback rushing yards this season.
Will Shipley, RB, EaglesAs of Monday night, we aren't projecting Saquon Barkley or Tank Bigsby to play for the Eagles in Week 5. That makes Shipley one of the biggest risers of the week, as I project him for 18 Fantasy points against Jacksonville. This isn't a good matchup, and the Eagles aren't currently a good offense, but any time a running back projects for this much work, he is going to be a top-30 running back. I would expect Shipley to score around eight Fantasy points without a touchdown, and if he scores, he'll be an RB2. He should be one of the most popular names on the waiver wire.RJ Harvey, RB, BroncosHarvey saw 10 targets in Week 4, which certainly moved his projection needle, even if we don't expect a repeat performance. The Broncos offense looks a little broken right now and Harvey has been more efficient running the ball than J.K. Dobbins. With Jonah Coleman on Injured Reserve, we expect Harvey's rush share to increase and he will probably be top three on the team in target share as well. He's a very good PPR flex this week against the Chargers.Ollie Gordon, RB, DolphinsIt was a wild week of speculation about the Dolphins running backs, but now we have some results. Gordon played 59.5% of the offensive snaps compared to Jaylen Wright's 29.7%. There was a similar split in rush share and surprisingly, Gordon also earned more targets. View him as a high-end flex who can be used as a low-end RB2 in a pinch. This is still a terrible offensive environment, but at least now we know who the lead back is. 
Malik Nabers, WR, GiantsNabers is the second guy who was a faller last week but rebounds as a riser in Week 5 after he broke out with six catches for 112 yards and a touchdown. I moved Nabers inside of my top 30 in this week's projections in what should be another good matchup. I may be a bit slower to move Nabers back into the top 20 because Jameis Winston still made a lot of bad throws against a bad defense and Isaiah Likely still dominated targets. Still, I suspect most people will feel comfortable starting Nabers in Week 5.Carnell Tate, WR, TitansTate had a monster Week 4 and now ranks 4th amongst all receivers with a 29.6% target share. He's also in the top 10 for first-read share. Cam Ward is making an effort to get his rookie receiver more involved and the results are promising. This is still a bad offense, but they did look slightly more competent against the Ravens in Week 4. Week 5 brings a bad matchup against the Texans, we think. The Texans have not played up to their reputation this season. I would start Tate as a low-end RW5 in Week 5.Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir, WR, BillsWe're expecting DJ Moore to take Week 5 off as he deals with a shoulder injury, which is a target boost to both Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir. For whatever it's worth, Coleman has been remarkably efficient and has seen a target share over 20% when Moore has been off the field. The third-year receiver has caught 14 of 16 targets and is averaging a ridiculous 13.6 yards per target. I would treat both of these guys as boom/bust WR3s in a bad matchup against the Rams.
FallersJalen Hurts, QB, EaglesEveryone is awful in Philadelphia. As of Monday night, we are projecting the team to be without Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, and Dallas Goedert. There are very few quarterbacks we would start without their top receiver, tight end, and running back, not to mention the fact that Landon Dickerson is on IR and Lane Johnson missed Week 4 for personal reasons. I don't want to drop Hurts, but I can't project him as a starter until he gets more help.David Montgomery, RB, TexansSince Week 1, Montgomery has 27 rush attempts for 67 yards. In those three games, he has scored 5.2 PPR Fantasy points per game, which ties him with Kyle Juszczyk for RB50. Over the last two weeks, it looks like Woody Marks has taken over work inside the 10, which was supposed to be the one thing that saved Montgomery. We'd take Marks straight up over Montgomery for the rest of the season, but neither looks like a Fantasy starter.Blake Corum, RB, RamsKyren Williams is playing excellent football and Sean McVay is rewarding him with more playing time, at the expense of Corum. In Week 4, Corum played a season-low 15.5% of the offensive snaps. This was the third time this year he's been below a 30% snap share. He's still one of the best handcuffs available, but he's no longer flexworthy alongside Williams.
Dalton Schultz, TE, TexansI leaned too heavily on Schultz's Week 1 targets in my Week 4 projections. With Nico Collins back, Schultz was an afterthought in the passing game, earning just two targets. He's still right around the TE12 range but needs to score some touchdowns to stay there. Unfortunately, Houston has rarely used him in that part of the field, as Schultz has scored just 10 touchdowns in 53 games with the team. Week 5 quarterback projections Week 5 running back projections  Week 5 wide receiver projections  Week 5 tight end projections

The semifinals tipped off Sunday, with both home teams getting big wins over their more proven opponents: the Dream defeated the Liberty 92-82 and the Valkyries' defense dominated the Aces' offense for a 71-60 win. All four teams now have a couple of days off, as both Game 2s of the best-of-five series won't tip off until Wednesday night. title: Coco Gauff responds to 'insane' racist remarks after China Open match - CBS Sports
description: America's highest-ranked singles player on the women's side described ugliness she encountered after the win
body:
America's highest-ranked singles player on the women's side described ugliness she encountered after the win
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:17 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        American women's tennis star Coco Gauff says she was bombarded with racially charged comments on social media this week following her 7-5, 6-1 third-round win over Sun Xinran in Beijing's China Open.Gauff stopped a rally during the first set after electronic advertising boards around the court flickered while striking a ball. Xinran, a 16-year-old sensation on the junior circuit, appeared to win the point before the chair umpire ruled the point should be replayed."Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff said in a reply on X after the match. "The amount of racist comments/DMs I've received in the last few hours is insane. Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief."Gauff, who's ranked No. 4 in the world after bowing out of last month's US Open in the semifinals, took control of the match from there and moved on to play Elise Mertens in Wednesday's Round of 16.In an Instagram post, Gauff detailed her reasoning for stopping the point.
"We are told before the matches we are allowed to continue to finish play so KEEP IT MIND I am thinking about all of this while i'm playing the point.," Gauff wrote. "Anything can be challenged after the point is over (as in most sports you can review a call after the play is over, I personally think is the correct rule). If I would've lost the point my opponent is also free to do the same thing and ask for a replay and she would've have been completely in her right to do so."She continued, "when it flickered again I raised my hands before she hit her shot because this is when I was sure I saw the light flicker and it wasn't my mind doing tricks lol (which again doesn't matter because anything can be challenged after the point)."Xinran won the junior US Open last month in New York and received a wild-card entry from tournament organizers. It was her official WTA Tour debut."It was an unfortunate situation but it is out of my control, the think pieces and calling me an unfair is ridiculous when those are the rules," Gauff wrote. "I did not make them, I think it's weird i'm getting hate for following the rules. Xinran is incredible talent and player, I apologized for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood. 
"I did not like to see her so emotional as l've been there and I really understand what it is like but this is just the beginning of an incredible career. It was an honor to share the court in front of her home crowd."

Jackson injured his ankle in the first half of Sunday's win over the Titans

        The Baltimore Ravens may be without their starting quarterback this weekend. According to a report from NFL Media, Lamar Jackson is dealing with an ankle sprain that gives him only an "outside chance" to play in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons. Jackson could miss multiple games depending on how his rehabilitation progresses, but the injury is not considered long-term or surgical, per NFL Media.Jackson got his ankle rolled up on the Ravens' final play of the first half during last week's win over the Tennessee Titans and did not return to the game. Ravens coach Jesse Minter initially seemed to suggest Jackson could have returned to the game had it not already been essentially in hand at the break, but this reporting makes that seem rather unlikely.The Ravens are 3-1 through the first four weeks of the season, and their offense has been highly explosive under new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. That's especially been the case in the three weeks Zay Flowers has been on the field, as Baltimore has averaged 33 points per game in those contests while scoring just 17 in a loss to the New Orleans Saints when Flowers sat out with a hamstring injury. If Jackson is unable to suit up for Week 5 and beyond, the Ravens will turn to backup Tyler Huntley. Huntley played the second half against Tennessee on Sunday and went 8-of-9 for 63 scoreless yards and ran four times for 16 yards. He's made 16 starts in his career, going 7-9. Across 31 total appearances, he's completed 66.6% of his passes at an average of 5.9 yards per attempt, with 13 touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
It's highly likely the Ravens will lean on their Derrick Henry-led rushing attack if Jackson has to miss time, but that could prove difficult in their game against the Falcons. Atlanta has lit up the scoreboard in each of the last two weeks and forced its opponents to play from behind. In such a scenario, it would be much more difficult for the Ravens to mount a comeback without Jackson at the helm.

Instead, they made three errors in the first inning of a 5-2 loss. The series will now shift to New York with the Yankees on the brink of elimination. Following a 4-3 loss to the White Sox in Game 2, the Guardians are in a similar boat, except they will have to stave off a sweep on the road. The Garrett Crochet trade is finally paying dividends in Chicago.The Falcons ran roughshod over the Saints. On an emotional night in New Orleans, the visiting team stole the spotlight. It started early when Bijan Robinson turned his first touch into a 59-yard touchdown, and the Falcons carved up the Saints on the ground for the rest of the night. The result was a big 45-24 win for Atlanta, and New Orleans won't enjoy looking at the film of this performance.Oregon QB Dante Moore returned to practice. The Ducks got a positive update on their starting quarterback just days before a top-25 matchup against UCLA. After suffering a concussion on a scary hit against USC, Moore returned to practice in pads and a helmet on Monday. We won't know Moore's official status for the game until later in the week, but this is a positive development. If Moore can't go, the Ducks will turn to Dylan Raiola, whose patience has already paid off.There are banged-up backfields in Philadelphia and Seattle. The Eagles may have avoided the worst-case scenario with Barkley, but he has still been labeled week-to-week while he recovers from a hamstring injury. The only backfield in worse shape than the Eagles' might be the Seahawks'. First-round rookie Jadarian Price is on IR with a chest injury, and Zach Charbonnet is still working his way back from a torn ACL he suffered last year. Because of that, the Seahawks turned to free agency and signed Joe Mixon off the street.Alex Ovechkin announced that the 2026-27 season will be his last. The NHL's all-time leading goal-scorer will retire at the end of the current season. In a video posted to social media by the Capitals, Ovechkin revealed his retirement plans to his teammates. Ovechkin's 929 goals are the most in NHL history, and no one is remotely close to his nine Rocket Richard Trophy wins. Ovechkin is now eyeing one more Stanley Cup after Washington loaded up in the offseason. 🏈 Do not miss this: UCLA rises in CFB Power Rankings

In fact, the Bruins are ranked even higher than that in Brandon Marcello's latest CFB Power Rankings. UCLA had an open date last week as it geared up for a top-25 game against Oregon this weekend, but it still climbed into the top 10 of our rankings. Not only does Chesney have the Bruins offense humming, but he also has the chance to get a little revenge after leading James Madison against the Ducks in last year's College Football Playoff. Marcello: "UCLA sat at home preparing for Oregon. James Madison's last three coaches - Curt Cignetti, Bob Chesney and current Dukes coach Billy Napier - are all unbeaten. Chesney returns this week to Eugene, where he led James Madison to a loss in the CFP's first round last season."Here's a little snippet of the complete rankings: 21. Virginia Tech (-1) 22. Houston (NR) 23. Iowa (-7) 24. Mississippi State (-13) 25. USC (-2) 
One team that's pretty far away from any top 10 ranking these days is Penn State, which is coming off a humiliating loss to Northwestern. The Nittany Lions plummeted 12 spots in the latest edition of the CBS Sports 138, and they're barely hanging on inside the top 50. Oh, and to make matters worse, Penn State is one of the 10 teams that landed on our Panic Meter after Week 5.  🏀 Ranking the NBA's best starting fives

In that regard, it's hard to beat the defending champion Knicks. Their quintet of oft-doubted stars returns after rolling to a title in last year's postseason. President of basketball operations Mike Gansey deserves a lot of credit for his summer masterclass. Gonzalez: "He flipped Paul George and his onerous contract for Brown, a Finals MVP who is coming off the best regular season of his career and is seven years younger. Then he convinced arguably the greatest player of all time to sign for the vet minimum with a team that hasn't made it out of the second round since 2001. That's some nifty maneuvering. Add them to a newly svelte Embiid and that blur of a backcourt and the Sixers suddenly boast their best starting five (yes, yes, still on paper) since Dr. J and Moses Malone delivered their last championship in 1983."Besides, the Knicks are currently in a contentious contract negotiation with a member of their starting five. According to Karl-Anthony Towns, extension talks "don't look good" with the season right around the corner. body:
There was a lot of turnover after the 2025 season, and several head coaches are already sitting on a pretty warm seat four games into 2026
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:07 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A total of 10 NFL head coaches were fired either during or at the conclusion of the 2025 season. While it's hard to fathom a similar amount of turnover this year, there are already several coaches who may be on the hot seat. We've ranked 10 NFL head coaches whose job security is either already in jeopardy or is on the verge of getting there. The list includes a former Super Bowl champion, a Super Bowl-winning coordinator, two coaches who recently led their teams to conference championship games and one first-year head coach. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Robert Saleh Seat temp. -- Cool Saleh knew he was signing up for a rebuild, and so far, the results have followed suit for the winless Titans. Each of Tennessee's last three losses was a one-score game, so Saleh and Co. appear to be heading in the right direction. Saleh is most likely safe this year, but some wins would make his standing for next year more secure. To do that, the Titans need to get more production from an offense that is currently 31st in the NFL in points scored. If Tennessee's offense doesn't improve, it could certainly lead to a change of coordinators this offseason. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Matt LaFleur Seat temp. -- Cool LaFleur's recent contract extension, which extends his deal through the 2029 season, is the biggest reason why he isn't ranked higher. The Packers are 2-7 in their last seven games and are 2-2 through the first four games of the 2026 season. Sunday's 17-14 win over the winless Buccaneers came at a cost as linebacker Edgerrin Cooper suffered what is expected to be a season-ending Achilles injury. Because of his contract, the only way LeFleur's job would actually be in jeopardy at season's end is if the Packers have an epic collapse and there are rumblings that he's lost the locker room. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. DeMeco Ryans Seat temp. -- Cool Unless you're a new coach or have a Super Bowl on your resume, being 0-4 usually means your seat is starting to get warm. Ryans, however, probably isn't there yet for several reasons. 
Ryans' Texans have reached the AFC divisional round three straight years. He's the NFL's only coach to win a playoff game each of the last three years. Houston is 0-4, but it finished last season with a 12-5 record after starting 0-3. The Texans play in the AFC's most winnable division, although the 3-1 Jaguars look formidable. Similar to LaFleur, Ryans should be safe this offseason, barring a truly horrendous campaign. One thing to consider, though, is the development of CJ Stroud and how much the Texans' brass will hold Ryans accountable if Stroud doesn't show enough improvement over the season's final three months. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Dan Quinn Seat temp. -- Room Quinn's time in D.C. is starting to mimic his time in Atlanta. He led the Falcons to a Super Bowl berth in his second season before things quickly went downhill. Washington came within a game of the Super Bowl in Quinn's first season, but it is just 6-15 since. 
Jayden Daniels' injury issues have plagued Washington, but it was 2-5 in games that Daniels played in last season. This season, the Commanders' defense has also been an issue as they are 31st in the league in points allowed. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Dan Campbell Seat temp. -- Room There's no denying Detroit's downward spiral since the departure of coordinators Ben Johnson and Aaron Glenn. The Lions are 11-10 since the start of the 2025 season. Ironically, the Lions' offense has continued to perform at a high level since Johnson left town. The issue has been Detroit's defense, or lack thereof. No team has allowed more points this season than the Lions, who are also 32nd in the league in passing yards allowed, third-down efficiency and red zone efficiency. 
Campbell did a masterful job restoring the roar in Detroit, but it's safe to wonder if they'll be able to get back to that point under his watch. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Shane Steichen Seat temp. -- Room Indianapolis has yet to make the playoffs under Steichen, who is in his fourth season as coach. It's fair to assume his job security will come into question if the Colts miss the playoffs this season. After a 0-2 start, the Colts have rebounded with wins over the Texans and Commanders. Sunday's game against the Steelers is the type of game Steichen and the Colts need to win if they want to get over the proverbial hump. Last year, Indianapolis came to Pittsburgh with a 7-2 record and lost a winnable game. It finished the season with an 8-9 record. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Nick Sirianni Seat temp. -- Tepid Sirianni's current situation embodies what it's like to be an NFL head coach, especially in the City of Brotherly Love. Sirianni has fallen out of favor in Philadelphia less than two years after winning a Super Bowl. Much of Sirianni's success and letdowns in Philadelphia have been tied to the play of Jalen Hurts. Hurts' early success led to Sirianni earning a ring and a contract extension after the 2024 season. Hurts and the offense's struggles, however, may ultimately lead to Sirianni's demise in Philadelphia. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Aaron Glenn Seat temp. -- Tepid If we only went off team performance, Glenn would definitely be on the hot seat. The Jets have lost three straight games and are 4-17 since the start of the 2025 season, Glenn's first in the Big Apple. 
Record aside, it appears that the Jets are content to give Glenn more time to turn things around. He's signed through the 2029 season, and, based on previous comments made by Woody Johnson, it seems that the Jets' owner wants to exude more patience this time around. A horrible season, however, might compel Johnson to make yet another coaching change. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Jim Harbaugh Seat temp. -- Warm Harbaugh was brought to Los Angeles to help Justin Herbert get to the next level. Instead, the Chargers have had two seasons without a playoff win and are currently 0-4. Herbert has taken a lot of the blame for the Chargers' current plight. Some of that criticism is warranted, but there's plenty of blame to go around. Herbert has had shaky pass protection, and his receiving corps is underwhelming. He also isn't meshing with Mike McDaniel. 
For those who think that Harbaugh's previous success might buy him more time, Chargers owner Dean Spanos infamously fired Marty Schottenheimer after a 14-2 season. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Todd Bowles Seat temp. -- Hot Following Tampa Bay's latest loss, Bucs Pro Bowl tackle Tristan Wirfs was asked what message he would relay to ownership regarding Bowles. "No comment," he said. "I love Coach Bowles. Yeah, I don't know." Wirfs' response basically sums up the situation in Tampa. Players may love Bowles, but the Buccaneers' ongoing struggles are what they are. The Buccaneers are 2-12 in their last 14 games dating back to last season. That ultimately falls on the head coach. 
In retrospect, the Buccaneers' offseason set them up for failure. They lost franchise icon Mike Evans after he signed with the 49ers. The Buccaneers then had to deal with the distraction of Baker Mayfield's contract extension, which didn't get done until September. It's a small sample size, but Mayfield has yet to live up to his new contract. Are all of these issues Bowels' fault? They aren't, but as noted above, a head coach is the person most responsible for the team's record. Heavy lies the crown, after all.

        One of the hallmarks of sports fandom these days is the compulsion to overreact to everything. The Florida Gators started the season 4-0. The Gators beat Auburn and then blew out an Ole Miss team coming off a win over LSU. The Gators were suddenly the hottest team in the country. A serious playoff contender.Then they went on the road and lost to Missouri 45-17, and they actually sucked the entire time. They were so overrated. Anybody who moved them into the top 10 in their opinion polls or power ratings is a clown and should feel stupid.When you do these power ratings, it's important to avoid overreacting to any single result. Crazy things happen in sports all the time, and typically, if the game spread is 5.5 points but the final score shows a 28-point deficit, it's an outlier result. It doesn't mean it isn't real, or that it was a fluke. It just means that, among the possible range of outcomes, the one we saw wasn't nearly as likely as many others.It doesn't mean Florida sucks. While the Gators drop a few spots in the ratings this week, their defense was already a concern last week, even though I had them at No. 9. I didn't downgrade it much this week. What was downgraded was the offense, because Missouri took away the run game, and Florida didn't have much of a counter. That's useful information.
Frankly, the real takeaway I had from the game was that I hadn't given Missouri nearly enough credit. I liked the offense already, but I was far too low on their defense. What the Tigers did in that game may have produced an outlier result, but it was no fluke. As a result, they don't crack the top 12 this week, but they're hovering. And honestly, given the way things have gone for teams ranked 11th and 12th in these ratings this season, the Tigers should probably thank me for not putting them there yet. I had Penn State at No. 12 two weeks ago, and look what's happened there.Now, if you want to talk about a team that may have sucked the entire time, Penn State's the team we should be talking about! That was a big swing-and-miss on my part, but hopefully it's been corrected going forward.Title odds via DraftKings.

title: How non-first round rookies are faring this NFL season: Denzel Boston among the leaders of the pack - CBS Sports
description: The NFL season is nearly a quarter complete, and several teams are already receiving good value on draft selections made in April. The f
body:
The NFL season is nearly a quarter complete, and several teams are already receiving good value on draft selections made in April. The first round represents roughly 12.5% of the selections made in the 2026 NFL Draft, and while they are considered the most likely to contribute early, teams fill out their roster with players selected in other rounds. Who are those non-first-round picks to take on an important role this season? There are 18 (8 on offense, 10 on defense) who have played 150+ offensive or defensive snaps through four weeks. It's an arbitrary number, but one that serves as a governor for the exercise. Among that sample size, there are six second-round picks, six third-round picks, three fourth-round picks, two fifth-round picks and one undrafted free agent. The undrafted free agent is Chiefs left tackle Kahlil Benson, whom I wrote about earlier this season. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LB Jaishawn Barham, Cowboys (Round 3, No. 92 overall)The Cowboys were an ideal landing spot for Barham because he had played both edge rusher and off-ball linebacker in college. New Dallas defensive coordinator Christian Parker studied under Vic Fangio with the Eagles. Over the past few years, Philadelphia has had a number of those body types with cross-trained backgrounds, such as Zack Baun, Jihaad Campbell, Nolan Smith, etc. With Barham, the athleticism jumps off the page, but there are still some inconsistencies in the run game. He has been credited with three pressures by TruMedia, but has not done as well at utilizing his quickness and setting up pass-rush moves as he did at Michigan. The production has been there early, but there is another level he can take his game when Parker grows more comfortable in his role. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    WR Denzel Boston, Browns (Round 2, No. 39 overall)Over the past decade, Boston has had the seventh-most receiving yards by a rookie through the first four weeks of the season. Ja'Marr Chase, Justin Jefferson and Puka Nacua are some of the notable names with more receiving yards as rookies through the first four games. TruMedia credits him with zero drops on the season. There have been a few that could have been categorized as such, but the defender was hanging all over him, and a penalty was not called. There were some missed connections with Deshaun Watson that could have manifested even better numbers. Boston is a big body who can win downfield, but what separates him is the attention to detail in his route-running. He can win at all three levels of the field. When the ball is not coming his way, he is a competent and willing blocker in the run game as well.He finished the pre-draft cycle as my No. 20 overall prospect. 
                                                                    TruMedia
                                                            Notably, Browns right guard Austin Barber is also one of the 18 rookies to meet the criteria. He has been very good despite making the transition from left tackle and looks like a long-term starter for the organization. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    CB Brandon Cisse, Packers (Round 2, No. 52 overall)Cisse builds speed quickly and is sticky in coverage. There was a blown coverage against Chicago where it looked like he was expecting safety help over the top, but otherwise, he rarely loses leverage. Cisse had Buccaneers rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels dead to rights in the backfield in Week 4, but he failed to complete the play. He has also not traveled from one side of the field to the other. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    WR Malachi Fields, Giants (Round 3, No. 74 overall)Fields has had two receptions and somewhere between two and six targets in each of his four games. On Sunday against the Cardinals, he scored his first touchdown. His two receptions were a byproduct of a lapse in coverage and a scramble drill. Individual catches against the Rams and the Cowboys better represented his potential. He has size and speed, but the route-running has been inconsistent. Fields does bring added value as a blocker in the run game. 
He has eight receptions for 126 yards and a touchdown. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LB Anthony Hill Jr., Titans (Round 2, No. 60 overall)Hill was one of my guys leading up to the 2026 NFL Draft. His athleticism is off the charts, and his ability to make an impact extends beyond playing in the box. The Texas product has the range to play sideline to sideline as well as the quickness to thrive as a spot rusher. Hill tends to get stuck on blocks in the box, and improving upon that will allow him to be more effective in fitting run gaps. Linebacker is a spot where experience is paramount, so starting early in his career allows him to troubleshoot some of his shortcomings, which will benefit him in the long run. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    WR Ted Hurst III, Buccaneers (Round 3, No. 84 overall)Hurst is more than a space eater in Tampa Bay's offense. He does a good job creating separation and covers ground quickly with long legs. On the season, he has eight receptions for 128 yards and one touchdown, but he had a few deep balls fall haplessly to the ground off his fingertips against Cleveland. Of note, seven of his eight receptions have come to the left side of the field. As the team battles injuries at the receiver position with Jalen McMillan and others, Hurst is a player worthy of a larger target share. 
The Buccaneers are now playing undrafted free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels in Baker Mayfield's absence. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    WR Bryce Lance, Saints (Round 4, No. 136 overall) The younger brother of Chargers quarterback Trey Lance has mostly been a sacrificial player for the Saints: clearing out defenders and blocking in the run game. He generally struggles to create separation, but he has been most effective planting and driving back toward the quarterback.Lance has four receptions for 50 yards on the year. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    CB Hezekiah Masses, Raiders (Round 5, No. 175 overall)Through the first two games, Masses had been targeted eight times and allowed one reception for 16 yards, according to TruMedia. He also had two interceptions in that time period. In Week 3 against the Saints, the rookie out of California was the victim of routes snapped off by Chris Olave. Masses allowed four receptions on the day — all by Olave — for 51 yards. Week 4 is where some of the concerns really took hold. His feet settled a bit at the stem, which enabled his assignment to gain separation, and there was a 42-yard gain to Tyquan Thornton. Masses' eyes lingered in the backfield, and Thornton caught him sleeping on a double move.
Nevertheless, Masses has the size and has met the physical challenge presented by the NFL. His awareness of what is happening around him and his ability to get his eyes back on the ball allow him to make game-changing plays. His performance should inspire confidence from the coaching staff. His potential was evident dating back to his time at Florida International and is one reason why he was a personal favorite in the pre-draft process. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    OG Emmanuel Pregnon, Jaguars (Round 3, No. 88 overall)The Jaguars offensive line was a potential problem area coming into the season, but the development of Pregnon, who was my No. 48 prospect overall, has brought stability to the unit. He has a wide, powerful body, and defensive tackles have had a difficult time playing through him; Bengals veterans Jonathan Allen and Dexter Lawrence were a few of the exceptions. Pregnon was inconsistent pulling and engaging blocks in open space, but he has shown improvement as recently as Sunday.TruMedia credits him with 0 sacks and 6 pressures allowed thus far.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LB Jacob Rodriguez, Dolphins (Round 2, No. 43 overall)Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley awarded Rodriguez the responsibility of serving as the green dot on defense as a rookie, meaning he communicates defensive calls to the rest of the unit. Rodriguez is an instinctual player who plays square to the line of scrimmage and displays the range to play sideline to sideline. 
One year after a fellow linebacker, Carson Schwesinger, broke the drought of linebackers winning Defensive Rookie of the Year, Rodriguez is on the path of building a case of his own. Through four games, he has 46 tackles, including three tackles for a loss and an interception. Among others in Miami, Dolphins' fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe also met the criteria. The five other rookies who have played at least 150 snaps, but were not represented on this list, are Buccaneers linebacker Josiah Trotter, Bears cornerback Malik Muhammad, Colts safety A.J. Haulcy, Panthers cornerback Will Lee III and Chargers center Jake Slaughter, who was called into action out of necessity when starter Tyler Biadasz suffered an injury.

title: SEC Power Rankings: Alabama leaps Georgia ahead of marquee showdown in Week 6 - CBS Sports
description: The Crimson Tide are making moves on the strength of an offense that has scored at least 45 points in every game
body:
The Crimson Tide are making moves on the strength of an offense that has scored at least 45 points in every game of its 5-0 start
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:38 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Going into Week 6, the SEC is a muddled mess. Teams in the middle of the pack are beating one another, and there's even a lack of clarity closer to the top.Georgia has steamrolled every team it's played so far, but its toughest opponents have been Oklahoma and Vanderbilt. Meanwhile, Alabama is also 5-0 with an offense that's been lighting the world on fire against mediocre to bad defenses.Luckily, we'll get some more insight into both teams when they meet in Tuscaloosa on Saturday night. For the time being, however, the Crismon Tide have leapfrogged the Bulldogs on the strength of their blowout victory over Mississippi State in Week 5. Keelon Russell and the Alabama passing attack looked unstoppable, but Kirby Smart has silenced plenty of explosive offenses in the past.Elsewhere around the conference, Florida got a dose of reality, and Will Stein kept his strong first season at Kentucky rolling with an exhilarating overtime win against South Carolina.
With another week of data points to work with, let's see how each team stacks up in the Week 6 SEC Power Rankings.
        
            
                CBS Sports 138: Alabama joins Texas, Georgia in top four as SEC teams headline college football rankings
                
                    Chip Patterson                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Texas Last week: 1The Longhorns got a week off before their rivalry clash against Oklahoma. Texas does have a little added pressure as it brings the No. 1 ranking into Dallas, but the Horns are the more complete team by a comfortable margin. That said, you have to expect the unexpected in the Red River Rivalry, so don't be shocked when John Mateer and the Sooners suddenly look like the Greatest Show on Turf.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Alabama Last week: 4It might be time to acknowledge that Alabama might just be an elite, national-championship caliber team. The Crimson Tide entered the season with some question marks, especially on offense, but they have answered all those questions in impressive fashion. This weekend's showdown against Georgia will be the real test, though. If Keelon Russell continues his heater against the Bulldogs, the Heisman hype train will be off the rails.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Georgia Last week: 2Georgia's slight dip is more about what Alabama has done and not what the Bulldogs have done wrong. After all, it was another week and another casual blowout for Georgia. The Bulldogs didn't exactly play a crisp game against Vanderbilt, but they still rolled to a 38-14 win. For the first time all season, Georgia won't be able to enter autopilot mode next when it visits Tuscaloosa. We know the Bulldogs are great. We'll know exactly how great they are at this time next week.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. LSU Last week: 6We didn't learn anything new about LSU in its beating of McNeese on Saturday, but what continues to stand out are Sam Leavitt's lapses, which seem to pop up every game. He's thrown an interception in every game, and he's up to seven interceptions on the season, which is tied for the most in the SEC. We'll see how Leavitt and the Tigers' offense operate on the road this week as they travel to Lexington for a matchup against Kentucky that looks much tougher now than it did prior to the season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Florida Last week: 3College football is a week-to-week sport, and Florida made that very clear in Week 5. The Gators were the talk of the town entering that matchup after a huge win over Ole Miss, and Missouri was a team full of question marks. Then the Tigers absolutely smashed the Gators, effectively derailing Jadan Baugh's Heisman Trophy campaign in three hours. Florida is still a very good team, but it's far from invincible.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Ole Miss Last week: 5Ole Miss got an open date to regroup after its loss to Florida, and it gets to dip its toe back into conference play with a matchup against Vanderbilt this weekend. Pete Golding has to find some band-aids for his run defense or the Rebels will get torched in the second half of their schedule.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Missouri Last week: 12Congratulations to the Tigers. They're the first team to make me look stupid, and it only took a week. Not only did Missouri beat Florida, but it dominated that game from start to finish. Austin Simmons got anything he wanted in the passing game, and the defense slammed the door on Florida's previously explosive run game. Vindication for Eli Drinkwitz. Now, can Missouri sustain this level of play?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Tennessee Last week: 8We have a full-blown quarterback controversy in Knoxville. Tennessee was headed for a devastating loss before Josh Heupel replaced Faizon Brandon with George MacIntyre, and that switch sparked the offense. Heupel is already tired of answering quarterback questions, but they're going to keep coming. How he approaches that position in a winnable game at Arkansas will be very telling.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Kentucky Last week: 10The Wildcats survived a road scare against South Carolina, and Will Stein's decision to go for the two-point conversion in the first overtime period paid off. Vibes are extremely high in Lexington these days, but those vibes are about to be tested. LSU is up next, and the last time Kentucky hosted a premier conference opponent, the result was a 45-17 loss to Alabama.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Mississippi State Last week: 7There was a reality check in Starkville last week. Mississippi State is a very good football team, especially with Kamario Taylor at quarterback, but it's still a couple of rungs below the SEC's elite tier. The Bulldogs will have to lick their wounds this week with a road trip to Death Valley on deck.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Oklahoma Last week: 9Brent Venables and Ben Arbuckle have gotten two weeks to fix whatever was ailing the offense, including the quarterback. If the Sooners can't get that side of the ball fixed, they'll be 2-3 leaving the Red River Rivalry, and Venables will face serious pressure to make staff changes.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Texas A&M Last week: 11Arkansas is the perfect elixir for struggling football teams. The Aggies got a relatively stress-free win over the Razorbacks, and Marcel Reed played a relatively clean game with 236 total yards and a touchdown. This weekend's game against Missouri is a fascinating matchup. Texas A&M has the talent to beat Missouri, but it's looked like a mess against quality opponents so far.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. Auburn Last week: 13Tennessee had zero passing yards for most of the first half, and Auburn still lost the game by 10 points. That's how ineffective the Tigers' offense was, and that's a big concern for Alex Golesh moving forward. The bad news is that Auburn's next game comes against Georgia. Hopefully, the Tigers' defense is up to the task because it will need to be.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    14. Vanderbilt Last week: 14Even with Jared Curtis sitting out due to injury, Vanderbilt managed to hang with Georgia for a half in an admirable effort. Blaze Berlowitz hit a couple of explosive plays in the passing game, but the Commodores ran out of steam. Vanderbilt will need Curtis next week to give it a puncher's chance at upsetting Ole Miss.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. South Carolina Last week: 15It feels like Shane Beamer sealed his fate when South Carolina blew yet another multi-score lead in an overtime loss to Kentucky. The Gamecocks won't be favored to win another game until they visit Arkansas on Nov. 14, so there should be plenty of opportunities for South Carolina to make a change if it wants.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. Arkansas Last week: 16When South Carolina is circling you as its next best opportunity for a win, you know things are bad. Then again, the Razorbacks do host Tennessee this week, and the Volunteers haven't won in Fayetteville since 2001.

title: Argentina after Miss: How do you replace the GOAT? - CBS Sports
description: The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner will play his final game for the national team on Tuesday
body:
The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner will play his final game for the national team on Tuesday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:03 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Tuesday, October 6, is going to be a historic day: Argentinian soccer star Lionel Messi, one of the greatest players in the history of the game, will play his final game with the national team after he announced his decision to retire from international soccer last month. Messi, who won two Copa Americas and the 2022 World Cup in Qatar with Argentina, will play his last match ever at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires and it's expected to be one of the biggest moments in his career. Many of his former teammates and current Argentina internationals will be in Buenos Aires to bid farewell to their idol. But with Messi's international career nearing its end, questions are already being raised about the future of the Albiceleste. Who will lead the next generation? Which players will follow Messi out of the national team? And what lies ahead for head coach Lionel Scaloni? Here's all you need to know. Who will follow Messi? The Argentinian national team will likely change a lot in the upcoming cycle that will lead to the 2030 World Cup that will be hosted by Spain, Morocco and Portugal. It's not clear yet which players are likely to follow Leo Messi's retirement, but players such as Nicolas Tagliafico, Nicolas Otamendi, Leandro Paredes and Rodrigo De Paul are unlikely to be part of the next tournament that will take place in four years. Even though there are still doubts over the matter, and no other player has officially announced their departure from the national team, it is easy to imagine that these players, who are particularly close to Messi both on and off the pitch, could also say goodbye to international soccer in the near future. This is a moment of change for the Argentinian national team, only a few weeks after losing the 2026 World Cup final to Spain and after the decision of Lionel Messi to leave the Albiceleste and play his farewell game on October 6. Who will lead the new cycle? Argentina have already announced their new captain for the upcoming cycle after Messi's retirement. Atletico Madrid defender Cristian Romero will be the new Argentinian captain, followed by Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez and Inter striker Lautaro Martinez. It's clear that no player will be able to replace the character of Messi on the pitch, and manager Lionel Scaloni will definitely have to rely on some new talents that have emerged over the last few years who could play in similar positions on the pitch. Real Madrid's loanee Franco Mastantuono was widely considered as one of the best emerging talents in Argentina when he was playing for River Plate before completing his move to the Spanish giants, but after some early struggles in his new team he recently moved on loan to Fiorentina where he's currently playing, hoping to gain his confidence back before making his way back to Real Madrid. Alongside Mastantuono, Como attacker Nico Paz is also one of the best Argentinian emerging talents right now.The 22-year-old Argentine was already called up by Scaloni for the 2026 World Cup, but from now on, he will be expected to take on a greater role as possibly the team's most talented and creative player. And while obviously nobody can replace Messi, he's probably the player with more expectations for the future. 
At the same time, Argentina can count on some crucial players that are part of the current roster that can lead the new cycle. Among them, Manchester City midfielder Enzo Fernandez, Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez and Inter captain Lautaro Martinez. Players who can, with their experience in the national team and in their clubs, help the new generation to integrate as soon as possible in the roster. Scaloni's biggest task It's never easy, historically, for a team to cope with the absence of such a legend of the game. It has happened in multiple sports, not only soccer, and will be no different for Argentina and their coach Lionel Scaloni. After the 2026 World Cup, there were also questions about the future of the manager, who raised doubts about his short-term future in the national team. Despite the rumours, the Argentine FA offered Scaloni a new deal until the 2030 World Cup, asking him to lead the project after the end of the Messi era, and according to the latest reports, he's now close to signing a new deal. Scaloni will have one main challenge to deal with, beyond the technical task of replacing Messi and coping with his absence. Since taking over as interim coach in 2018, Scaloni has had to manage the pressure surrounding Messi, who had previously endured a difficult period with the national team and struggled to deliver major trophies. Step by step, Scaloni helped Messi to achieve his dreams and won the 2022 World Cup as well, but all the players who played in the national team since he was the manager all worked together to help their captain to achieve his childhood dreams. All egos, individual targets, and personal ambitions were left behind to help Messi. Looking back, players weren't celebrating for themselves but for Messi. When Lautaro Martinez scored the winning goal in the semifinal earlier this year against England, completing an incredible comeback in the last minutes of the game, the whole team ran to Messi, including Lautaro himself. A celebration that tells us how much he was loved and respected in the squad.
From now on, things will be different. Egos, individual ambitions and strong personalities will inevitably come back, and it will be up to Scaloni and the team's most experienced players to manage them and keep Argentina united without their leader and most important player.

body:
Welcome to Week 5 of the NFL season, which is always my favorite week because it's when I finally come to grips with the fact that my Fantasy team is absolutely horrible. I only do four leagues every year and the one where I ALWAYS do the worst is my work league here at CBS Sports. I always get the worst draft slot and I always end up with the worst team and even if my team is somehow good, it doesn't matter, because everyone is eventually going to get injured. For instance, I have Saquon Barkley on my team this year, and he's already injured. In 2024, I had Christian McCaffrey. Last season, I had Brock Purdy. If I draft a player in my fantasy league, there's an 89% chance he's going to get hurt. If any NFL players are reading, I will accept money next year NOT to draft you. That way, you don't have to worry about getting injured. I'm a walking jinx. By the way, if anyone in my league is reading, Barkley is officially on the trade block and I will take anything for him. I'm thinking Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson for Barkley straight up. Please let me know if you're interested. 
Anyway, the only thing I'm interested in right now is getting to the Week 5 picks, so let's do it. Actually, before we get to the picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here, but you don't need to click over this week, because we have more important things to go over right now, like why you should sign up for the Pick Six newsletter that we have here at CBSSports.com. Based on my unscientific research, I've found that roughly 52.3% of the people who read this picks column wish they could get an email from me twice a week. Well, YOU CAN. I write the Pick Six NFL newsletter here at CBS Sports and it comes out twice a week (Monday and Thursday). If you want it sent to your inbox, all you have to do is click here and subscribe. Once you sign up, you'll immediately start getting the newsletter where I'll be touching on every NFL-related topic I can think of and even ones that I can't think of. If you're wondering how that's possible, you'll have to subscribe to find out. 
Alright, I'm going to stop talking so we can get to the picks. All lines via DraftKings; All times ETNFL Week 5 picksRaiders (3-1) at Patriots (2-2)Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS,  Stream on Paramount+)After watching Drake Maye play over the past four weeks, I feel like I can pretty confidently say that this game is going to go one of two ways for him: Either he's going to turn the ball over seven times and the Patriots are going to lose by 21 points or he's going to throw for 278 yards and three touchdowns in a wild win that no one saw coming. There is no in-between. Maye is a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside an enigma. I can't figure him out, you can't figure him out, Mike Vrabel can't figure him out. No one can figure him out. One week, he might show up and play like Tom Brady. Another week, he might show up and go full Ryan Leaf. It can't be easy for Josh McDaniels to create an offensive game plan when he doesn't know which Maye is going to show up. 
The good news for the Patriots is that it might not matter this week because they shouldn't have to TOTALLY lean on Maye against the Raiders' defense. The Raiders are 3-1, but if they've had one issue on defense this year, it's that they haven't been able to stop the run. They did hold the Dolphins to just 74 yards on the ground in Week 1, but that came against the Dolphins, so I'm not going to count that. In the three games since then, they've given up an average of 154.7 yards per game, which is the most in the NFL over the past three weeks. The only other defense that's given up at least 150 yards per game in that span is the Packers, and if you've watched the Packers play defense at all this season, you know that being compared to them is not a good thing. And we haven't even gotten to the ugly part for the Raiders. The ugly part is that they're giving up 5.2 yards per carry. The Raiders' pass-rush has looked fantastic this season -- the Vegas defense has registered at least two sacks in each game this year -- but if the Patriots run the ball on every play, then they won't have to worry about the pass-rush. 
This feels like a game where Maye will be asked ot throw 20 or 25 passes and then McDaniels is going to let his two running backs (Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson) do the rest. The Raiders are definitely a good team, but I just don't like this spot for them: They're coming off a tough loss to a division rival, and now, they have to fly all the way across the country. Also, the Raiders beat Mike Vrabel in his first game ever as the Patriots' coach last season, and he seems like the kind of guy who would hold a grudge over that. PICK: Patriots 27-24 over Raiders (+3.5)Bears (3-1) at Packers (2-2)Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo -- try for free)I don't think it's mathematically possible to be eliminated from the division race after just five weeks, but if the Packers lose here, I'm writing them off. And yes, if they lose here and then somehow end up winning the division, I definitely expect you to send this to that Old Takes Exposed guy so he can make fun of me.
The Packers are sitting at just 2-2, even though they were gifted one of the easiest QB slates to start the season. Here's who Green Bay has faced so far: Week 1: Carson Wentz/Kyler Murray (Murray got knocked out of the game in the first quarter)Week 2: Geno SmithWeek 3: Michael Penix Jr. (He was making his first start in nine months)Week 4: Jalon Daniels (He's an undrafted rookie who was making his first career start)If the Bears were playing this schedule, they would have put up 65 points on the Jets in Week 2 while starting their fourth-string QB, because that's what the Bears do, but that's not what the Packers do. Green Bay is 2-2, and the scary part is that the Packers are about three plays away from being 0-4. Both of their wins came by exactly three points. 
So why have the Packers been struggling? Someone could probably write a book on this, but I don't have time for that, so I'll try to do the quick summary: Their offensive line is a mess, they can't run the ball and Jordan Love hasn't looked great, but that's not completely his fault because he usually only has roughly 0.7 seconds to throw, because, again, the offensive line is a mess.If the Packers could run the ball, that would help fix a lot of their problems, so let's check in to see how their rushing attack is doing this year without Josh Jacobs, who's currently on the commissioner exempt list. 
Oh. If you're ranked 32nd, that means no one is worse than you and that's a lot of things to be ranked 32nd in. 
And then you have the Bears, who are the complete opposite of the Packers. Ben Johnson has designed such a perfect offense that it doesn't even matter who's under center. The Bears were down to their third-string QB (Case Keenum) in Week 3 and they still put up 375 yards of offense, which is more than the Packers have put up in three of their four games this year. In Week 4, Johnson gave the starting QB job to someone else (Tyson Bagent) and the Bears racked up nearly 500 yards of offense. At this point, I'm convinced that the Bears could start an actual bear at quarterback and the offense would still be serviceable. So Johnson has the better offense, and also, he hates the Packers. 
We need more head coaches who hate their division rivals. There was a game back in 1989 where Bengals coach Sam Wyche called a timeout with under 20 seconds left to play so he could kick a field goal. His team was up 58-7. He wanted to hit 60 points. The Bengals won 61-7. I could see Ben Johnson doing that (And shout out to my dad, former NFL kicker JIm Breech, for drilling the field goal)
The Packers' season isn't over if they lose here, but I think we'll be able to throw their division title hopes out the window. PICK: Bears (-3) 30-23 over Packers49ers (4-0) at Seahawks (3-1)Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo -- try for free)We are four weeks into the NFL season and no one has figured out how to stop the 49ers offense yet. In Week 1, the 49ers took a mini-vacation to Australia and then capped that vacation by dropping 27 points on the Rams. In Week 2, the 49ers scored 35 points before the end of the third quarter, but then took their foot off the gas against the Dolphins. In Week 3, Brock Purdy carved up the Cardinals' defense for four touchdowns in a game where the 49ers ended up scoring 36 points. In Week 4, the 49ers hit a road bump in the first half against the Broncos before exploding for 21 points in the second half. Through four weeks, the 49ers are the second-highest scoring team in the NFL. They're averaging 30.5 points per game and if they get to 30 in Seattle, they're going to win, because the 49ers do NOT lose shootouts. Since the start of the 2021 season, the 49ers are 37-1 when they score 30 points or more, including the playoffs. 
That being said, if anyone can hold the 49ers to under 30 points, it's the Seahawks, who have one of the best defenses in the NFL. Not only that, but they have a defensive mastermind in Mike Macdonald, who is the one head coach you want to have when you're facing a Kyle Shanahan offense. In his two seasons on the job, Macdonald has faced the 49ers five times, including one game in the playoffs, and the 49ers have only topped 30 points one time (and that came in Macdonald's first meeting with them, a game the Seahawks lost 36-20). In the four games since then, the 49ers haven't even hit the 20-point mark, and they've averaged just 10.8 points in those four games. This coaching matchup is basically like watching Garry Kasparov vs. Magnus Carlsen play each other in chess. I don't know if they've ever actually faced each other, but those are the only two chess names I know outside of Bobby Fischer, so we're going to stick with them. Shanahan will adjust to whatever Macdonald's been doing and then Macdonald will adjust to Shanahan's adjustments. It's a never-ending battle of wits. If Shanahan has one advantage going into this game, it's that Brock Purdy is playing the best football of his career. The 49ers QB hasn't been sacked a single time this season, marking just the third time in the Super Bowl era that a QB has led his team to a 4-0 start without being sacked. The only other quarterbacks to pull that off were Dan Marino for the 1984 Dolphins and Peyton Manning for the 2005 Colts. If you're doing things that only Marino and Manning have done, I can't pick against you. Purdy was my preseason pick to win MVP last year, and he's doing everything now that I thought he'd do in 2025. I hate making predictions. Although Lumen Field can get loud, no one has been able to handle that better than Purdy, who has the best record (4-1) of any visiting QB in Seattle. I think this is going to be a tight game, but I'm riding with the 49ers. Shanahan is going to use Purdy to put the Seahawks in checkmate. And that will probably be the final chess reference of the year. Sorry, chess nerds.  PICK: 49ers (+2.5) 27-24 over SeahawksRavens (3-1) at Falcons (2-2)Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET (NBC, Stream: Fubo -- try for free)I don't usually put much stock in home-field advantage, but I have decided that I am NOT going to pick against the home team anymore on Sunday Night Football or any game on NBC. Through the first four weeks, here's what's happened in each NBC game: Week 1: New England at Seattle (-2.5) -- Seahawks win 13-10 (Wednesday night opener)Week 1: Dallas at N.Y. Giants (+3) -- Giants win 28-20 Week 2: Indianapolis at Kansas City (-6) -- Chiefs win 33-30Week 3: L.A. Rams at Denver (+2.5) -- Broncos win 30-26Week 4: Detroit at Carolina (+3.5) -- Panthers win 32-26There have been five NBC games and the home team has won all of them, including three games where the home team was an underdog. Lamar Jackson is dealing with an ankle injury, so I don't know if he'll play in this game, but I don't care. I'm not picking against the home team. The NBC jinx is real and the Ravens are up next. One reason the Falcons might be able to win here is because the Ravens are extremely banged up. Not only is Jackson dealing with an ankle injury, but several key players, including CB Marlon Humphrey (calf) and guard Andrew Vorhees (foot) were knocked out of Baltimore's Week 3 win over the Titans. Also, the Falcons have finally figured out how to play football. During the first two weeks of the season, they were stuck playing Cooper Rush at quarterback and that didn't work out so well for them. However, things have quickly turned around with Michael Penix under center. In Penix's two starts, the Falcons have averaged 40 points and 459 yards per game. No one can tackle Bijan Robinson. No one can cover Drake London. And Michael Penix actually looks like he knows what he's doing. He's making the right reads, he's getting the ball out quickly and he's throwing accurately. Penix only has four starts in his career where he's completed at least 70% of his passes, and two of them came in his two games this year. Even if this NBC jinx didn't exist, I'd probably still take the Falcons, but it does exist, so I don't any choice here. PICK: Falcons (+2.5) 30-27 over RavensBills (3-1) at Rams (2-2)Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET (ESPN, Stream: Fubo -- try for free)After four weeks of Monday night blowouts, the Bills and Rams are here to save Monday Night Football. If you've been falling asleep at halftime of every Monday game this season, I can't blame you and that's because every single game has been unwatchable in the second half. Week 1: Chiefs 31-10 over Broncos Week 2: Rams 28-6 over Giants Week 3: Bears 27-7 over Eagles Week 4: Falcons 45-24 over SaintsThe games have been so bad that I've used the second half of each game to teach myself how to knit. That's now what I do with my Monday nights, but there will be no knitting this week. When I saw this game on the schedule back in August, I thought it looked like a potential Super Bowl preview, but after watching these two teams play for the past four weeks, I'm not so sure. The Bills are 3-1, but those three wins have come against three teams that are a combined 2-10. The Bills' best win came against a Lions team that currently has the NFL's worst defense. I'm not saying I'm concerned about the Bills just yet, but I'm not saying I'm not. I think what I'm trying to say is that I'm somewhat worried about this team and that's mostly because the defense can't stop anyone. The Patriots offense had scored a total of 29 points through the first three weeks and they hit that number in ONE game against the BillsThe Bills have given up the sixth-most passing yards in the NFL this season, and now, they have to face the reigning MVP (Matthew Stafford) and they have to figure out how to stop both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. This is a nightmare matchup for the Bills and if they had anyone besides Josh Allen at quarterback, I'dl probably pick the Rams by double digits, but they have Josh Allen. The last time the Bills played the Rams came two years ago, and it played out a lot like I expect things to play out on Sunday: The Bills' defense got steamrolled, but Buffalo still almost won thanks to a superhuman performance from Josh Allen, who totaled SIX TOUCHDOWNS. 
I'm expecting more of the same this week, but I could see that turnover number going up. Allen has made some questionable throws in big spots this year. In Week 4, he threw an interception that iced the win for the Patriots in a situation where the Bills only needed about 15 more yards to get into range for a possible game-tying field goal. In Week 1, the Bills would have lost to the Texans if Kamari Lassiter hadn't dropped a gift of an interception with under two minutes left to play. 
Allen can't afford to turn the ball over against the Rams because the Bills' defense just isn't good enough to bail him out against good teams. Heading into Week 4, the Bills were on top of the AFC East and they looked unbeatable, but things could soon get very interesting. If they lose this game, and the Patriots beat the Raiders, New England will suddenly take over first place in the division. This is a big game for both teams, but I feel like the Rams need it more, so I'm rolling with them.  PICK: Rams (-2.5) 34-31 over BillsNFL Week 5 picks: All the restCowboys 27-17 over BuccaneersJaguars 30-20 over EaglesBears 23-20 over PackersTexans 20-13 over TitansBengals 24-16 over DolphinsVikings 19-16 over SaintsBrowns 20-17 over JetsColts 22-19 over Steelers Giants 23-16 over CommandersBroncos 27-20 over ChargersLions 30-23 over CardinalsBYES: Chiefs, PanthersLast Week Best pick: Browns over Steelers. Last week, I predicted that the Browns would beat the Steelers by three points in a thriller and guess what happened? The Browns beat the Steelers by exactly three points in a thriller. Now, did I know that Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy were going to cuss each other out DURING the game? Of course. Rodgers and McCarthy are like a divorced couple who decided they're going to stay together until their youngest kid graduates high school.  
They don't necessarily want to be in this together, but at this point, it's pretty clear that it's the only option. 
Also, I picked the Browns to win because they're basically unbeatable on Thursday nights and that's when this game was played. I'm not sure the NFL would agree to it, but the Browns should definitely ask the league to schedule all of their games for Thursday night next season. Worst pick: Jets over Bears. The Jets have been bad for so long that I usually just automatically pick against them each week without even thinking about it, but for some reason, I strayed from that plan. In Week 4, I decided the Jets were going to pull off an upset against the Bears, and let me just say, that absolutely backfired in my face. Aaron Glenn and Ben Johnson spent four seasons together in Detroit, so I thought maybe that would help Glenn when it came time to scheming up a defensive game plan that might be able to slow down the Bears, but I was wrong. In a wild coincidence, the team (Browns) from my best pick of the week is playing the team (Jets) from my worst pick of the week this Sunday. I bet you can guess who I'm taking. Hint: It's not the Jets. Picks recordStraight up in Week 4: 10-6SU overall: 38-26Against the spread in Week 4: 6-9-1ATS overall: 28-34-2BREECHIGAMIS: 1You can find John Breech on Facebook or Twitter, and if he's not doing one of those things, he's sitting in a dark corner somewhere regretting every Jets pick that he's ever made in his life.

title: NBA head coach rankings: Where all 30 stand entering the 2026-27 season - CBS Sports
description: There is no harder group to evaluate in professional basketball than the coaches. It's not a single job. It's a dozen tied together by a
body:
There is no harder group to evaluate in professional basketball than the coaches. It's not a single job. It's a dozen tied together by a title. You're a strategist and a therapist and a human resources manager and a public relations official and a split-second decision-maker all rolled into one, and you almost never get credit for it because most of the job is invisible. For players, the whole job is on display. For coaches, most of it is getting those players ready and keeping them engaged behind closed doors.As I point out every year, any attempt to rank them is at best an incomplete endeavor and at worst, closer to a futile one. They're all juggling hundreds of decisions we don't get to see, yet we judge them on the few that we do. They're all working with different resources, and they're all kept on increasingly short leashes. We didn't quite reach the heights of stunning coaching turnover we saw in 2024 and 2025, but in fairness, that's because most of the accomplished coaches had already been fired. Erik Spoelstra and Steve Kerr are the only remaining coaches in the NBA hired before the start of this decade. Only eight sitting head coaches have held their posts for the last four full seasons. The coach is almost always the fall guy when things go wrong. Every coach is either on the hot seat or a bad year away from getting there. It may not be totally fair for us to judge coaching performance, but it's not as though teams tend to judge coaches fairly either.So what can we judge when it comes to coaches? These are the traits that come to mind:
Track record. This is obvious. A great coach tends to win a lot of games in the regular season and advance deep into the postseason.Performance against expectations. Sometimes, a great coach is stricken with a limited roster. Can he make lemonade out of those lemons? Some coaches happen to consistently find themselves with elite talent. What does it say about them if they can't make the most of it?Points of emphasis. Do your teams take the right kinds of shots? Do they allow the right kinds of shots? Do you have ways of generating turnovers without excessive fouling? Do you balance rebounding and transition on both ends of the floor? Essentially, is your team doing the right things on paper? Are you plucking the low-hanging fruit?Creativity. Have you found unorthodox uses for under-valued players? Are there things that you do that other coaches don't? Can you draw up a nice out-of-bounds play?Player development. Do your draft picks pan out? Do you find productive players on the margins? Do players leave your team and get better? Do players leave your team and get worse?Rotation management. Are you playing the right players? Are you overusing your best players? Are you underusing them? Do you have specific lineup quirks that help or hurt your team consistently?People management. Again, we are working with very limited information here, but based on what we can see, do your players like you? Do they play hard for you? Are you operating in lockstep with your GM? Are you constantly battling with ownership? Can you manage the politics of your locker room?There is no set rubric here. There are, however, a few traits I'm choosing to emphasize this year. The first is playoff performance. Every April, we're reminded of how different the regular season and postseasons actually are. A coach consistently winning in January means less to me if he consistently comes up short in April and May. The second is recent performance. The NBA changes quickly and coaches need to be able to adapt with it. If a coach had a particularly shaky year last season, that's going to factor in heavily here. Those are the coaches with the most to prove this season.Before we begin, I open each list with the same, all-important qualifier: there are far more good coaches than bad ones in the modern NBA Teams are getting better and better at identifying strong candidates, and the correlation between coaching acumen and job security is distressingly inconsistent. Winning in the NBA has much more to do with players than coaches. Most of these coaches could succeed with the right players. Only a few of them actually have them. There is no curve on this list. Most sitting NBA head coaches are good at what they do, but somebody has to populate the lower end of the list. With that in mind, let's start ranking.
