Spoelstra's after-timeout numbers have always been a bit underwhelming relative to expectations. Miami's game management hasn't been quite as bulletproof in recent years as it was in the past. Spoelstra even pulled a Chris Webber and called a timeout the Heat didn't have in 2024. He and the next two coaches are in a tier, but our top two picks have just had more recent success. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Mark Daigneault, ThunderLast season's rank: 6Notably, NBA players voted Daigneault the NBA's best coach in 2025 through The Athletic's annual poll. He came up just behind Mazzulla last season. Oklahoma City's culture is renowned across the sport, and it seemingly carries the Thunder no matter who's on the floor. The Thunder without Shai Gilgeous-Alexander last season still had a net rating that would've placed them in the top-10 in the league across the full season, and they're 22-19 without their MVP across the past four seasons. The Thunder were among the first teams to truly embrace the importance of turnover margin and have built their historic defense around steals and the fast-break points they generate. Practically every player this coaching staff touches turns to gold.If there's a question here, it comes down to separating organization from coaching staff. The measure of a coach -- at least in a strategic sense -- is his ability to solve problems, and the Thunder are usually at such a talent advantage that problems scarcely arrive. They did in the Western Conference Finals due to injury. The Thunder lost. Daigneault's 2025 championship run was littered with questionable decisions. His "foul up-three" approach cost the Thunder Game 1 against the Nuggets, and changing his starting lineup before the Finals was an unforced error. Daigneault has built an almost impenetrable structure in Oklahoma City. The Thunder are a machine. He just hasn't built the sort of strategic track record our No. 1 pick has.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Rick Carlisle, PacersLast season's rank: 1Ignore everything you saw last season, or at least remember that all of that misery was the result of Carlisle taking a No. 4 seed to Game 7 of the NBA Finals in the first place. Carlisle has always been a playoff overachiever. Think of the stars he left in his wake on the way to the 2011 title. No team pushed the 2014 Spurs further than Carlisle's Mavericks did as a No. 8 seed. There is no better playoff tactician than Carlisle. He once nearly stole a playoff series by surprisingly inserting Boban Marjanović into the starting lineup after spending most of the season without him even in the rotation. He'll try anything, and almost everything he tries winds up working.That's his single best trait as a coach. Carlisle is as stylistically flexible as any coach in basketball. He's built dominant offenses around Luka Dončić dribbling the air out of the ball, and he's built dominant offenses around Tyrese Haliburton's up-tempo passing machine. He disarmed LeBron James in the Finals with Tyson Chandler and a zone. He looked at his 2024 roster, realized the defensive personnel wasn't good enough, shrugged and seemingly just decided "well, if we can't guard anywhere, we can at least run everybody off the line and give up the fewest 3s in basketball." The Pacers made the conference finals, so clearly, it worked. If you need a single basket, he might be the coach you choose to draw up the play. His full-court football sets are downright beautiful. The Pacers built their roster around second-draft players like Haliburton, Aaron Nesmith and Obi Toppin. If that doesn't sell you on his player-development track record, the memory that he was Jalen Brunson's first NBA coach should.The last time we saw Carlisle in serious games, he was out-coaching the No. 2 finisher on this list. Carlisle pushed Daigneault to the brink despite an inferior roster and a lower seed. That's all he ever does. He's never had the sort of undeniable rosters that most Hall of Fame coaches get, but his teams are universally scarier than they have any right to be simply because he's the one leading them from the sidelines.

title: Tyler Shough reacts to fans booing after Saints blowout loss to Falcons: 'I'd boo, too' - CBS Sports
description: New Orleans was blown out by the Falcons on 'Monday Night Football'
body:
New Orleans was blown out by the Falcons on 'Monday Night Football'
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:28 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New Orleans Saints were run out of their own building on Monday night as the Atlanta Falcons steamrolled their division rival to a 45-24 victory in Week 4. Given that this is one of the most venomous rivalries in the league, Saints fans weren't happy to see such a lopsided result, especially on a night celebrating the 20th anniversary of the return to the Superdome following Hurricane Katrina. And they let the team have it, with boos raining down from the stands. "Fans understandably are upset," quarterback Tyler Shough said postgame, via ESPN. "We had some opportunities that we didn't take advantage of, and you're playing the Falcons, and you lose like that. I mean, I'd boo, too. That sucks."
The game wasn't particularly close, with the Falcons almost instantly jumping out to a 14-0 first-quarter lead. Over that same stretch as Atlanta punched it into the end zone twice, New Orleans went three-and-out, missed a field goal, and fumbled. By halftime, that grew to a 24-7 lead, and Atlanta was effectively off to the races from there.Cam Jordan candidly said that New Orleans got "punched in the mouth early" and the Falcons "had their way today."
The loss dropped the Saints to 1-3 on the season, leaving them looking up at both the Panthers and Falcons, who finished the first month of the regular season at 2-2. "I'm disappointed. More than anything, you lose to the Falcons like that and especially on a Monday night game, it sucks," said Shough, who dropped to 0-3 in his career against the Falcons on Monday. "There's nothing you can say, like, 'Ah man, it doesn't suck.' It definitely does. But I do know as a team that we're extremely close, and we're going to keep going and keep our eyes forward. "We have really good leadership, and our leadership on the team admits that we got to get better... There's no hiding that. But at the same time, it is a long season, and there's a lot of games yet to be played to where we can do that."
Saints' coach Kellen Moore agreed. He called the game "disappointing" for several reasons, including the fact that it was a Monday night matchup with a crowd ready to roll."The dome was an incredible night, incredible energy," Moore said. "Didn't coach well enough; didn't play well enough. Obviously, it wasn't good enough."It's just disappointing for us, and I know there's frustration for everyone." The Saints will try to bounce back on a short week as they remain in New Orleans and gear up for a Week 5 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

title: Why Josh Allen's, Bills' 3-1 start isn't as impressive as it seems - CBS Sports
description: The Buffalo Bills started the season 3-1. Impressive right? Well, maybe not as impressive as it seems.Buffalo is currently atop the AFC
body:
The Buffalo Bills started the season 3-1. Impressive right? Well, maybe not as impressive as it seems.Buffalo is currently atop the AFC East, ahead of the 2-2 New England Patriots, 1-3 New York Jets and 0-4 Miami Dolphins. So far, the Bills' schedule hasn't been difficult, and even with easier opponents, their games have been close — and in some areas, sloppy. The teams they've defeated have a combined record of 2-10. That's not great. It seems that each year, there are debates about whether an AFC East team is good or if its schedule just makes it look good. Currently, it's the Bills at the center of that conversation. Turnovers have been an issue for former MVP Josh Allen and Co., and their pass defense is in the bottom five in the league. They've allowed 29-plus points in three of their four games, and there have been a lot of missed chances.
There's no argument that the Bills don't have their moments of brilliance, or good numbers in many categories, but let's look at who they are playing well against (and who they lost to). Buffalo's one loss came to the New England Patriots, who were accused last season of looking only as good as they did because of an easy schedule. They seemingly proved those doubters right by starting this season (with a much harder schedule) in disastrous fashion.Let's not be too dramatic — the Bills are far from terrible, and they'll be in the playoffs this year. But as great as the Bills have been on paper in the Allen Era, they have yet to even make a Super Bowl, never mind win one. If they're going to make it happen this year, they can't compare themselves against sub-par teams.Buffalo's record is deceiving, so let's start from the beginning of the season and work our way to this week, diving into each matchup.
Week 1 vs. TexansBills 36, Texans 31The Houston Texans are currently 0-4 and back in their season opener, the Bills beat them by less than a touchdown. The Texans outplayed the Bills by several metrics: More first downs (Bills 20, Texans 26)Better third-down conversion percentage (Bills 0/3, Texans 7/16)Better fourth down conversion percentage (Bills 0/1, Texans 2/2)Better red zone conversion percentage (Bills 1/3, Texans 4/5)Won the time of possession battle (Bills 23:43, Texans 36:17)More rushing yards (Bills 86, Texans 124)Of all categories Buffalo won, many were close. The Texans are one of the worst teams in football, and even in Week 1, the Bills should've had a more dominant victory. Week 2 vs. LionsBills 41, Lions 31This win was a bit more comfortable at 10 points, and overall, the Bills had a stronger performance. No one is questioning whether Allen is putting up big numbers, but against the opponents they've faced, we should be seeing more blowouts.
The win marked Buffalo's first in their new stadium and was Allen's sixth career five-touchdown performance. The Lions are the best opponent the Bills have beaten (that is, the only opponent they've defeated who has won a game this season).From such a hyped up team, giving up 31 points in each of the first two weeks is notable.Week 3 vs. ChargersBills 24, Chargers 16The Chargers are one of the most frustrating teams in the league and one of the worst, sitting at 0-4 with more problems than they can begin to solve.
The Bills had five turnovers against the Chargers, with three fumbles lost and two interceptions thrown, and Allen didn't have a passing touchdown. And this game was in Buffalo! If it were against a team with even an ounce more competency, the Bills would be sitting at 2-2 right now. It's as if L.A. wanted to lose the game, because historically, teams that turn the ball over five times don't come out with a check in the win column. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert had his best game in terms of passing yards against the Bills with 226, and it is the second-most points put up by L.A. so far this season.Allen did have two rushing TDs, and the Bills' defense picked off Herbert, though that's not too rare (he has six interceptions this season). It wasn't bad for the Bills in every category, but look who it was against.
Week 4 vs. PatriotsPatriots 29, Bills 26Heading into this game, the defending AFC champions looked broken. People were calling the Patriots one of the worst teams in the league, quarterback Drake Maye was playing so poorly that people were nicknaming him "Fake Maye," and they were making far too many mistakes in all three phases.The Bills came into this game undefeated with home-field advantage, but it didn't matter.Maye, who entered the game with one touchdown and six interceptions, outplayed Allen. The Patriots QB finished with 269 yards, three touchdowns, one interception and one fumble, while Allen had 253 yards, one touchdown in the air, one on the ground and one interception.
Allen and his receivers didn't even have the challenge of facing Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez, who was out with an injury. Defensive tackle Christian Barmore was also out, but the Patriots' defense still managed to look complete without two of their biggest stars.Maye was better with his legs than Allen, who is known for his ability to extend plays on the run. Maye had 54 yards on the ground on eight carries, while Allen had four yards on five carries. The numbers don't lie, but the eye test doesn't either. Maye had a number of impressive plays, including one when it mattered most. He capped off an eight-play 73-yard drive with a dime to Efton Chism, who made an incredible one-handed grab to put the Pats up 29-26 with just under two minutes to go.
The game is never over when Allen has the ball. However, he all but sealed the loss by throwing an interception with 1:14 to go. One play doesn't lose a game, but it's mistakes like that, especially against a depleted defense, that Allen can't be making.The Patriots had a combined 29 offensive points going into Sunday. Yes, combined from their first three games, and they were able to match that against Buffalo's defense.Looking aheadThe Bills will now head to L.A. to play the struggling Rams next week, who barely beat a shaky Philadelphia Eagles team in Week 4. Even if they defeat the Rams, the Eagles' opponents will have a combined record of 4-13. It's a long season, but Allen and Co. have plenty to fix if they want to make their Super Bowl window.
